summary: Store plan step 5: encrypted transport for the phones. The desktop phone endpoint and the headless server mint one self-signed certificate per install (data dir, tls/), reuse it across restarts, and serve wss:// and ws:// on the same port (the first byte of a connection picks TLS or plain). The pairing QR keeps its ws:// address and adds the certificate's SHA-256 as fp, so older phones ignore it and keep ws://. Native Android pins fp, dials wss:// on the same port, treats a changed certificate as a terminal error that asks for a re-pair, and in release builds refuses plain ws:// to any host but loopback and the emulator host (network security config and a clear message). The Expo iOS app cannot pin without a native module: it keeps fp in the saved address, and App Store and TestFlight builds refuse plain ws:// to a remote host, so they reach a backend over Cloud IAP or a wss:// address with a system-trusted certificate until a pinning module ships.

automated: vitest tests/unit/backend-tls.test.ts: the certificate verifies against its own key, its SHA-256 matches the stored fingerprint, the key file is 0600, a restart reuses it and an unreadable one is replaced; one port answers ws:// and wss:// with the pinned certificate; close releases the port for a restart.
vitest tests/unit/transport-security.test.ts: the QR URL carries fp, the Expo parser keeps it lowercase and refuses a malformed one, and the cleartext rule allows only wss://, loopback and 10.0.2.2.
jest apps/mobile transport-gate.test.ts: an App Store build refuses remote ws:// before any dial and shows the reason, an internal build dials as before, an unreadable build type fails closed.

Gradle :app:testDebugUnitTest: PinnedTlsTest dials a MockWebServer over TLS with a certificate made by the desktop generator (match opens, mismatch is CertificateChangedFailure), pairing parse upgrades a pinned ws:// QR to wss://, the resolver refuses remote ws:// in release mode, and the status copy for a changed certificate.
Gradle lintDebug assembleRelease: the release APK packs the TLS-only network security config, debug the permissive one.
npm run typecheck and npm test pass.
notExercised: Not run on a physical phone or an emulator, and not against a running desktop app: the wss:// path was exercised only by the tests above.
iOS pinning is not built: React Native's WebSocket cannot pin, so it needs a native module and a new iOS build.
The Settings > Mobile QR was not checked visually; only its URL string changed.
